evidence.title: Tangier Departure (June 1325 CE): Legal Scholar Sets Out for Mecca
evidence.dateBasis: Rihla departure chronology (2 Rajab 725 AH)
evidence.summary: At age twenty-one, Marinid Maliki scholar Shams al-Din Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Battuta left Tangier eastward along the Maghrebi coast toward Tunis and Egypt.
evidence.limits: Dating of early stages relies on the dictated Rihla of 1355–1356 by Ibn Juzayy, occasionally telescoped across itineraries.

evidence.title: Alexandria & Mamluk Cairo (1326 CE): Nilometer, Colleges & Red Sea Corridor
evidence.dateBasis: Mamluk Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad chronology & Rihla account
evidence.summary: Ibn Battuta admired Alexandria’s Pharos harbor, Mamluk Cairo’s towering hospitals and madrasas, and took the Upper Egyptian Aidhab route before war rerouted him via Syria.
evidence.limits: Crowd estimates and distances combine direct eyewitness observations with literary topoi of Islamic geographical adab.

evidence.title: Damascus & Mecca Hajj (1326–1330 CE): Scholarly Network & First Pilgrimage
evidence.dateBasis: Damascus ijazah diplomas & consecutive Meccan Hijri years
evidence.summary: Joined the Levantine caravan out of Damascus and resided nearly three years in Mecca, studying Malikite law and acquiring credentials that opened judicial posts across Asia.
evidence.limits: Chronology of his side excursion to Ilkhanid Iraq and Shiraz shows hindsight edits in manuscript recensions.

evidence.title: Zeila, Mogadishu & Mombasa (1331 CE): Benadir Cotton Textiles & Somali Coast
evidence.dateBasis: Winter NE monsoon sailings in the Rihla & Swahili-Benadir urban archaeology
evidence.summary: Sailing down the Red Sea past Yemen, Ibn Battuta praised Mogadishu’s sultanate hospitality, spiced meat-and-rice banquets, and woven Benadir cloth exported to Egypt.
evidence.limits: Coastal visits depended on seasonal monsoon delays rather than extended overland interior exploration.

evidence.title: Kilwa Kisiwani (1331 CE): Southernmost East African Monsoon Harbor
evidence.dateBasis: Mahdali Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulaiman Husuni Kubwa contemporaneity
evidence.summary: Described Kilwa as one of the finest coral-and-timber towns seen anywhere, ruled by Sultan Abu al-Mawahib and funded by inland Zimbabwe gold and elephant ivory.
evidence.limits: Did not penetrate inland beyond the coral island town to see Great Zimbabwe’s dry-stone capital.

evidence.title: Hormuz, Anatolia & Kipchak Steppe (1332–1333 CE): Pearl Fishery to Golden Horde
evidence.dateBasis: Corroborated Ilkhanid, Aydinid & Khan Uzbek court synchronisms
evidence.summary: Crossed Oman and Hormuz before traversing Anatolian beyliks, Crimea, Khan Uzbek’s steppe camp, and briefly accompanying Princess Bayalun to Byzantine Constantinople.
evidence.limits: Sequence around Bulgar in northern Russia is suspected by historians as partly synthesized from second-hand fur-trade tales.

evidence.title: Delhi Imperial Court (1334–1341 CE): Qadi under Sultan Muhammad ibn Tughluq
evidence.dateBasis: Barani & Isami Delhi Sultanate chronicles intersecting Rihla years
evidence.summary: Served nearly eight years in Delhi as richly salaried Maliki qadi and administrator of Sultan Qutb al-Din’s mausoleum amidst court opulence, famines, and imperial rebellions.
evidence.limits: Court anecdotes emphasize Ibn Battuta’s personal survival through volatile sultanate purges.

evidence.title: Maldives Atoll Qadi & Cowrie-Coir Hub (1343–1344 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Dynastic Sultanate chronicles (Tarikh) of Malé confirming queen Khadija
evidence.summary: Briefly served as chief judge in Malé amidst cowrie-shell currency exports (sent onward to Bengal and West Africa), dried skipjack tuna, and coconut coir ship-ropes.
evidence.limits: Naval shipwreck off Malabar prior to arriving stripped him of his original Delhi embassy gifts.

evidence.title: Pasai & Zaytun / Quanzhou (1345–1346 CE): Muslim Diaspora Quarter in Yuan China
evidence.dateBasis: Yuan Maritime Customs context, Pasai tombstone synchronisms & Rihla report
evidence.summary: Sailed aboard massive Chinese-built merchant junks past Samudera Pasai to Zaytun (Quanzhou), marveling at silk, paper money, porcelain, and self-governing Hui Muslim port quarters.
evidence.limits: Claimed northern overland side trip to Khanbaliq (Beijing) is debated by scholars due to compressed chronological inconsistencies.

evidence.title: Taghaza, Walata & Niani Royal Mali Court (1352–1353 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Sultan Mansa Sulayman reign dates & Mali royal griot protocols
evidence.summary: After surviving the 1348 Black Death in Syria and returning to Fez, dispatched south across Taghaza salt pans into Mali Empire, witnessing Mansa Sulayman’s gold-bow court and Niger towns.
evidence.limits: Oral-imperial capital location of Mansa Sulayman’s Mali (Niani vs alternate Upper Niger sites) remains archaeologically discussed.

evidence.title: Berenike Troglodytica (Red Sea Coast, Egypt): Greco-Roman Teak & Pepper Port
evidence.dateBasis: 7.55 kg Indian black-pepper jar, Tamil-Brahmi ostraca & teak timbers
evidence.summary: Arid Red Sea desert harbor yielding Indian Malabar black pepper, Sri Lankan sapphire/garnet beads, Indian cotton sails, and Tamil-Brahmi inscribed storage pots.
evidence.limits: Roman port abandonment after c. 550 CE left upper Byzantine strata exposed to wind erosion.

evidence.title: Adulis Harbour (Gulf of Zula, Eritrea): Aksumite Ivory & Monsoon Gateway
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified Aksumite mint issues, Aila-Aqaba amphorae & Periplus records
evidence.summary: Premier Aksumite maritime gateway linking Ethiopian highland ivory, gold, and obsidian to Egyptian grain wine jars and western Indian Ocean ships.
evidence.limits: Seventh-century coastal silting and Islamic-era shoreline shift curtailed major port activity.

evidence.title: Qana (Bi’r ‘Ali) & Khor Rori (Hadramawt–Dhofar, Arabian Sea): Frankincense Harbors
evidence.dateBasis: Himyarite–Hadhrami inscriptions, basalt ballast & Indian cooking pots
evidence.summary: Southern Arabian fortified coastal hubs stockpiling Dhofar Boswellia sacra frankincense resin for Red Sea galleys and monsoon freighters waiting out seasonal wind shifts.
evidence.limits: Khor Rori siltation closed the natural estuarine lagoon around the 5th–6th centuries CE.

evidence.title: Muziris / Pattanam (Periyar Delta, Kerala): Pepper, Gems & Monsoon Landfall
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Roman amphorae, Mediterranean glass, Indo-Pacific beads & river dugout
evidence.summary: Primary western Indian landfall for June–August Southwest monsoon ships returning with silver denarii, glass, and frankincense in exchange for Malabar black pepper, beryl, and cardamom.
evidence.limits: Shifting Periyar delta floods in 1341 CE submerged and migrated historical river channels.

evidence.title: Shanga & Kilwa Kisiwani (Swahili Coast): Sewn Dhows, Timber & East African Gold
evidence.dateBasis: Coral-built Friday mosques, Persian Siraf jars & Kilwa minted copper-gold coins
evidence.summary: Seasonal Northeast trade winds brought Gulf dhows to Lamu, Manda, and Kilwa every winter carrying Basra turquoise jars, returning northward on summer winds with mangrove poles, ivory, and Sofala gold.
evidence.limits: Acidic tidal muds rapidly decompose wooden sewn-plank hulls compared to coral-stone architecture.

evidence.title: Siraf & Old Hormuz (Persian Gulf): Maritime Dhow Warehouses & Pearl Divers
evidence.dateBasis: Excavated Siraf coral-gypsum merchant residences, Chinese Yue greenware & weights
evidence.summary: Abbasid–Buyid coastal merchant metropolis built in desert cliffs above Persian Gulf shipping lanes, channeling Changsha bowls and Samarra lustrewares directly to Canton and East Africa.
evidence.limits: Severe earthquake of 977 CE and Buyid decline shifted trade southeastward to Kish and Hormuz.

evidence.title: Palembang & Muaro Jambi (Sumatra): Srivijaya Straits-Monsoon Holding Port
evidence.dateBasis: Sabukingking Old Malay inscriptions, Changsha sherds & Belitung-era shipping
evidence.summary: Sumatran riverine thalassocracy perfectly sited where Northeast and Southwest monsoons forced transshipping ships to pause and exchange spice-island cloves, camphor, and sandalwood.
evidence.limits: Low-lying Musi River alluvial wetlands preserve brick stupas and pilings sparsely below modern silt.

evidence.title: Calicut (Kozhikode, Kerala): Zamorin Entrepôt & Karimi Spice Brokers
evidence.dateBasis: Ming Zheng He stone records, Zamorin port copper-plates & Karimi archives
evidence.summary: Open surf roadstead governed by the Zamorin under strict neutral customs, connecting Aden–Hormuz–Cairo Karimi merchants with Chinese ocean fleets and Southeast Asian spices.
evidence.limits: Lack of a sheltered harbor bay meant vessels anchored offshore according to strict seasonal windows.

evidence.title: Melaka Sultanate (1400–1511 CE): Maritime Law Codes & Syahbandar Port
evidence.dateBasis: Undang-Undang Laut Melaka maritime statutes & Ryukyuan/Ming custom records
evidence.summary: Multi-ethnic emporium run by four port masters (syahbandar) for Gujarati, Kalinga, Javanese, and Chinese merchants timed strictly to annual opposing monsoon switches.
evidence.limits: Portuguese 1511 stone fort construction obliterated much of the timber sultanate palace precinct.

evidence.title: Quanzhou (Zaytun, Fujian): Shipwrecked Spice Cargoes & Maritime Mosque Stelae
evidence.dateBasis: 1277 Houzhu Song shipwreck pine hull holding pepper, ambergris & turtle shell
evidence.summary: Song–Yuan oceanic port hosting Tamil Hindu stone carvings, Ashab Mosque Kufic stelae, and water-tight bulkhead merchant hulls excavated with intact Indonesian spice cargoes.
evidence.limits: Mid-14th-century Ispah rebellion and early Ming sea-ban (haijin) curtailed direct private voyages.

evidence.title: Shum Laka & Cameroon Grassfields Origin Matrix (2000 BCE–1 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Stratified basalt stone hoes, early oil-palm ceramics & aDNA baselines
evidence.summary: Northwest Cameroonian Grassfields highland edge corresponding to Proto-Bantu linguistic diversity and pearl-millet/yam-oil-palm transitions prior to southward dispersal.
evidence.limits: Excavated ancient individuals at Shum Laka matched deep Central African foragers rather than incoming Bantu farmers, showing mosaic population adjacency.

evidence.title: Obobogo & Okolo Forest Pits (Central Cameroon, 1000–400 BCE)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS oil-palm nuts, pearl millet grains (c. 400 BCE) & flat-based jar pits
evidence.summary: Southern Cameroonian rainforest villages cutting deep rubbish pits packed with domesticated pearl millet, oil-palm kernels, polished stone axes, and early iron slag.
evidence.limits: Organic rainforest acidity destroys skeletal fauna across open-air pit settlements.

evidence.title: Lopé, Okanda & Ogooué Savanna–Rainforest Corridor (Gabon, 500 BCE–600 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Okanda bloomery furnaces, charred Raphia–Canarium kernels & charcoal chronology
evidence.summary: Central African savanna corridor along the Ogooué River tracking Early Iron Age villagers clearing forest margins before regional demographic decline around 400–600 CE.
evidence.limits: Radiocarbon curve plateaus and summed-probability dips debate abandonment vs mobile resettlement.

evidence.title: Imbonga, Pikunda & Munda Sangha Riverine Corridor (Middle Congo, 400 BCE–500 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Comb-stamped river-levee ceramics, iron bloomery & inner-basin boat surveys
evidence.summary: Canoe-borne ironworking fishing communities following Congo and Ruki-Sangha riverbanks straight through equatorial flooded forest during seasonal low-water windows.
evidence.limits: Seasonal river flood erosion destroys long stratigraphic sequences along low levees.

evidence.title: UreweDimple-Based Pottery & Great Lakes Early Ironworking (500 BCE–500 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Brick tuyere conical furnaces (Rugomora Mahe), pearl millet & sorghum AMS
evidence.summary: Kagera and Nyanza Iron Age agriculturalists firing distinctive dimple-based Urewe vessels beside high-temperature brick smelting furnaces, radiating into Eastern and Southern Africa.
evidence.limits: Multiple interaction fronts with Nilo-Saharan cattle herders created diverse highland cultural blends.

evidence.title: Kwale Coastal Hill Villages & Urewe–Kwale Derivative Expansion (100–500 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Fluted-rim Kwale bowls, iron slag heaps & East Coast settlement spread
evidence.summary: Early Eastern Stream Bantu-speaking ironworkers settling coastal monsoon hills near Mombasa and rapidly expanding south down littoral Mozambique and inland plateaus.
evidence.limits: Limited coastal human bone preservation constrains direct early Eastern Stream aDNA.

evidence.title: Silver Leaves, Matola & Lydenburg Heads (Limpopo–Mozambique, 250–700 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: AMS shell/charcoal dates on Matola ware & hollow Lydenburg terracotta heads
evidence.summary: Coastal Mozambique dunes and Mpumalanga valley villages proving rapid southwards arrival of ironworking Bantu farming and ceremonial terracotta sculpture by the 3rd–6th centuries CE.
evidence.limits: Interaction with ancestral Khoekhoe–San herders and foragers leaves clear genetic admixture signatures.

evidence.title: Schroda, K2 & Mapungubwe Hill (Shashe–Limpopo, 900–1290 CE)
evidence.dateBasis: Gold rhinoceros sanctuary burials, Žhizo glass-bead sequences & terraced stone
evidence.summary: Sacral kingship center emerging out of Southern African Bantu cattle-farming chiefdoms, exporting hammered river gold and carved ivory along Limpopo trails to Indian Ocean dhows.
evidence.limits: Climate desiccation around 1290 CE saw elites abandon the Limpopo valley in favor of Great Zimbabwe.

waves.title: Ibn Battuta leg 1: Tangier via Cairo & Damascus to Mecca (1325–1326 CE)
waves.summary: Marinid scholarly pilgrimage corridor connecting Mediterranean North Africa with Mamluk Syria and the Hijaz.
waves.limits: Schematic itinerary along recorded Rihla stopping towns.

waves.title: Ibn Battuta leg 2: Aden & Mogadishu to Kilwa & Hormuz (1331–1332 CE)
waves.summary: Red Sea and East African monsoon voyage connecting the Arabian Peninsula directly with Swahili coral ports down to Kilwa.

waves.title: Ibn Battuta leg 3: Hormuz via Steppe & Delhi through Maldives to Quanzhou (1333–1346 CE)
waves.summary: Transcontinental passage through Transoxiana to Delhi Sultanate service and eastward diplomatic sea voyage to Fujian.
waves.limits: Malabar shipwreck interrupted original overland Bengal route before continuing maritime sail.

waves.title: Ibn Battuta leg 4: Fez across Taghaza Salt Route to Niani & Timbuktu (1352–1353 CE)
waves.summary: Royal Marinid commission traversing Taghaza salt slabs to Mali’s court and the Middle Niger bend.
waves.limits: Return camel track via Takedda copper mines.

waves.title: Western Indian Ocean Monsoon Loop: Red Sea–East Africa–Malabar (100 BCE–700 CE)
waves.summary: Classical open-ocean monsoon crossings harnessing June–August Southwest winds toward India and December Northeast winds back to Red Sea ports.
waves.limits: Schematic monsoon shipping belt rather than fixed sea lane.

waves.title: Gulf–Swahili Dhow Corridor: Siraf & Hormuz to Lamu & Kilwa (750–1500 CE)
waves.summary: Annual dhow rhythm carrying ceramics, dates, and cloth south while hauling East African mangrove rafters, ivory, and Sofala gold north.
waves.limits: Seasonally reversible wind lane along Somali–Zanj literal currents.

waves.title: Bay of Bengal–Malacca Transshipment Axis: Kozhikode to Palembang & Quanzhou (670–1500 CE)
waves.summary: Connected segmented sailing system meeting at Srivijaya and Melaka where sailors waited between opposing Bengal and South China Sea monsoons.
waves.limits: Voyages routinely transshipped cargoes across Malay–Sumatran entrepôts.

waves.title: Western–Rainforest Bantu Frontier: Grassfields through Cameroon to Ogooué (1500 BCE–200 CE)
waves.summary: Expansion of Bantu-speaking yams, oil-palm, and pottery communities south along coastal savanna corridors and river valleys.
waves.limits: Represents cumulative multi-century demographic expansion routes modeled by phylogeography and archaeology.

waves.title: Inner Congo Basin Riverine Corridor: Sangha & Congo Waterways (400 BCE–500 CE)
waves.summary: Rapid river-canoe penetration carrying Imbonga–Pikunda ceramics and bloomery iron into central-eastern Congolian basins prior to ~400 CE shifts.
waves.limits: Schematic arterial river network inferred from levee excavations.

waves.title: Eastern Stream Bantu Arc: Great Lakes Urewe to Kwale Coast (500 BCE–500 CE)
waves.summary: High-temperature brick-furnace ironworking and millet-sorghum Urewe communities moving east toward Kilimanjaro and Kenya littoral hills.
waves.limits: Combines linguistic Eastern-Bantu branching with dated ceramic horizons.

waves.title: Southern Coastal–Plateau Stream: Kwale & Matola to Mapungubwe (250–1200 CE)
waves.summary: Rapid coastal and riverine dispersal into Mozambique, Transvaal, and Limpopo cattle-farming and gold-trade societies.
waves.limits: Genomic admixture models indicate integration with southern Khoe-San foraging and pastoralist groups.

studies.title: Ibn Battuta: Across Dar al-Islam & the Indian Ocean (1325–1354 CE)
studies.summary: Follow Tangier legal scholar Ibn Battuta through 29 years of travel across Mamluk Cairo, Mogadishu, Kilwa, Kipchak steppe, Delhi Sultanate, the Maldives, Yuan Quanzhou, and Mansa Sulayman’s Mali Empire.

studies.title: Indian Ocean Monsoon World: Spice, Gold & Sewn Ships (100 BCE–1500 CE)
studies.summary: Trace how predictable seasonal monsoon wind reversals integrated Egypt’s Red Sea ports, Aksum, Hadramawt, Malabar pepper coasts, Swahili Kilwa, Siraf, Srivijaya, Melaka, and Song–Yuan Quanzhou centuries before European sails.

studies.title: The Bantu Expansion: Farming, Iron & Languages Across Sub-Saharan Africa
studies.summary: Explore genomic, linguistic, and radiocarbon evidence tracking Bantu-speaking agricultural and ironworking societies from the Cameroon Grassfields through the Congo rainforest corridors, Great Lakes Urewe furnaces, and Limpopo–Mapungubwe.
